setup_note: Logged-in personal account → Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps → 'Register a new OAuth app'. Four fields (name, homepage URL, optional description, redirect URI) plus three checkboxes. Client ID shown immediately on 'Application created successfully'; client secret via a separate 'Generate a new client secret' button. No review, no waiting, no email.
registration_access_claim: Any logged-in GitHub user can register an OAuth App from Settings → Developer settings; no organization, verification or payment needed.
approval_claim: The app was usable the moment it was created. The only review-like thing on the page is an optional 'List this application in the Marketplace' button; nothing requires it.
unreviewed_limits: No limits shown at creation. The app page shows '0 users' and a 'Revoke all user tokens' control; no test-user cap or scope restrictions were mentioned.
redirect_uri_rules: The form allows up to 10 redirect URIs. http://localhost:8000/callback was accepted without any HTTPS warning. An optional 'Allow wildcard matching' checkbox (off by default) extends a URI to subdomains and additional paths; without it, matching is exact.
token_lifecycle: Expiring tokens are a per-app option: the 'Expire user access tokens' checkbox is OFF by default. The form says enabling it 'will provide a refresh_token which can be used to request an updated access token when this access token expires'. With it off, tokens do not expire.

blockers.blocker: Device flow is off by default; a CLI/agent that uses the device authorization grant gets an error until 'Enable Device Flow' is ticked.
blockers.fix: Tick 'Enable Device Flow' on the app's settings page (it can be changed after creation).

blockers.blocker: Expecting a refresh_token when 'Expire user access tokens' is off (the default).
blockers.fix: Tick 'Expire user access tokens' if your agent handles refresh; leave it off if it expects a long-lived token.

notes: The form is at github.com/settings/applications/new; the created app lives at github.com/settings/applications/<id> with General, Optional features and Advanced tabs.
Three checkboxes on the form: 'Allow wildcard matching' (per redirect URI), 'Enable Device Flow', 'Expire user access tokens'. All three are unticked by default.
No mention anywhere of HTTPS being required, of app verification, or of scope-based review.
Corrects the generated guide: it claimed one redirect URI per app, exact match only, and (in one run) that expiring tokens are on by default.
